findings.evidence: The same runner facts are stated three or more times: 'Check the active runner's line-2 template= header, never the .new file' (268), again in the ensure-runner row (352) and the NEVER item (375-377), plus runner.md; the trusted-root decline refusal is explained at 142-148 and again at 296-300
findings.fix: State each fact once (the .new/template-8 readiness rule in 'Cross-AI execution', the trusted-root refusal in 'Skills') and let the subcommand row and the NEVER item point to that section in a few words

findings.evidence: Step 3 says 'Resolve each choice with plan-set or decline it with plan-unset' but gives no order, although choices depend on each other: the runner model depends on 'script:cross-ai.runtime', and declining a trusted root is refused 'while agents still hold the skills it covers'
findings.fix: Add a resolve order at the top of step 3: 1) script:cross-ai.runtime, then script:cross-ai.model.<runner> (or set workflow.cross_ai_execution false); 2) agent_skills.<agent> lists; 3) the trusted root (approve, or decline only after step 2 dropped its skills); 4) the pi steer; then re-run the dry run

findings.evidence: 'Never delete an apply marker without following the recovery text apply prints.' gives no reason. Environment gotchas (pi PI_PROVIDER only set for the agent's bash tool at 136-137, the opencode bare profile still loading ~/.agents/skills at 250-251, resolve_model_ids: omit emptying resolve-model at 159-161) are scattered with no Gotchas list
findings.fix: Add the reason: 'the marker records the only recovery steps for a half-restored config and is what blocks a second apply over it'. Collect the scattered environment facts into a short Gotchas list next to NEVER

findings.evidence: The description spends words on mechanics ('v2 flow — inventory, recommend, plan edits, apply, follow-ups; the kept v1 path asks only model_profile'), has no trigger for requests that do not name the config file, and names a boundary only against gsd-settings, while it claims to 'set up ... cross-AI plan review' next to ai-kit-spec-review and ai-kit-cross-ai
findings.fix: Set up or migrate a GSD project's `.planning/config.json` the curated way: pick models per tier, wire installed skills to GSD agents, and configure cross-AI plan review and a cross-AI execution runner (`cross-ai.mjs`), through an inventory, a reviewable plan, a dry run and an apply. Use when asked to configure .planning/config.json, set up GSD config fast, pick GSD models or rigor, wire skills to GSD agents, migrate a v1-curated config to v2, set up or upgrade a cross-AI execution runner (render cross-ai.mjs, ensure-runner, merge cross-ai.mjs.new), or set the pi session steer, even when the user only says 'get GSD going on this repo' without naming the config file. Not for tuning single advanced knobs (gsd-settings/gsd-config), running a cross-AI review of a plan or spec (ai-kit-spec-review), or dispatching a model call through the runner (ai-kit-cross-ai).

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 411 lines of dense prose, by line-length estimate well above the about-5000-token body guideline. Reference-grade blocks load on every run: the reference resolution and refusal checks (279-318), the Limits table (331-340), the runner exit-code list (40-45). runner.md's 'Do NOT load for the stock v2 flow' (runner.md:7) is visible only after loading it, and runner.md chains on to ../../ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md
findings.fix: Move lines 279-318 into references/skills-wiring.md, loaded when plan-set/apply refuses an agent_skills entry or a skill_unwired note appears. Move the runner exit codes into runner.md. Put 'Do NOT load runner.md for the stock v2 flow' at SKILL.md 269-273, and leave one-line pointers in place

findings.evidence: model_profile marks 'adaptive recommended', but rigor is offered as three equal options ('mvp ... standard ... or rigorous') with no default, so the agent cannot advise a user who asks which to pick
findings.fix: Mark a default, for example 'standard (recommended)', and add one line on when to pick the others: mvp for throwaway or cost-capped work, rigorous when planning errors are expensive and two review lanes are available

findings.evidence: 16 queries. The negatives have no keyword overlap ('explain how the Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaler...', 'generate a Mermaid sequence diagram...'), none are near-misses for gsd-settings, ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-cross-ai, and every positive names the domain outright with no file paths or casual phrasing
findings.fix: Reach about 20 queries. Add near-miss negatives ('turn off workflow.research in my GSD settings', 'run a cross-AI review of PLAN.md now', 'dispatch this task to codex through cross-ai.mjs', 'install GSD into this repo'). Add 2-3 implicit positives with realistic context ('new repo at ~/code/shop, get GSD going with cheap models and my installed skills')

findings.evidence: Assertions are hard to verify: 'asks only the choices it cannot resolve itself and does not ask a long list of questions' (12) and 'renders the runner through the cross-AI build step' (32), a step SKILL.md never names. 5 of 6 evals list no input files
findings.fix: Make them checkable: 'asks exactly the four questions (model_profile, rigor, cross-AI review, cross-AI execution) in one message'; 'apply writes .planning/scripts/cross-ai.mjs and sets workflow.cross_ai_command to node .planning/scripts/cross-ai.mjs'. Attach an inventory fixture under evals/files/ to the cross-AI and opencode evals

findings.evidence: 'This skill never dispatches a model call: check a runner with --print-argv only. A live dispatch runs with full permissions and only when the user asks for one.' The second sentence contradicts the first, so the agent cannot tell whether to run a dispatch the user asks for
findings.fix: This skill starts no model call on its own; check a runner with --print-argv. Run a live dispatch only when the user explicitly asks for one, and say first that it runs with full permissions.

findings.evidence: 'WORK="$(mktemp -d)"' creates a scratch dir, and the Reporting rule says to 'keep the files in $WORK', but no step ever ends its life, so every run leaves inventory.json and plan.json in the temp dir
findings.fix: Add to step 6: after the follow-ups, give the user the $WORK path, and remove it once they no longer need the JSON (keep it when an apply failed or a marker remains)
